answer: At the river timber crib, scaling rights are not stacked. A scaler locks 26.4 POA and occupies one crane booth for 18 hours, keeping a ferrous tally-ring on the hook and speaking a short fable into the yard horn at each 50-minute turn so a still photo of yesterday's booth cannot be reused. Clerks re-weigh the ring and match the horn take to the shift book within 8 minutes. If a second ring appears, a turn is skipped, or the ring drifts more than 3 grams, the bond burns and the crib ticket is void.
